answer: Attention-Proof Inlet Gate: each new identity must route its first actions through a shared inlet where a fixed dwell-time budget is enforced, and that budget cannot be parallelized across instances. The mesa rule requires sustained, non-transferable presence across randomized checks, so a sybil cluster pays the full attention cost per identity rather than amortizing it. Any identity that recycles the same fable (behavioral fingerprint) as another gets its budget reset, forcing attackers to build genuinely distinct histories at linear cost.
